name: Andaman Fish Curry
description: The everyday island staple: same-day fish such as snapper, tuna or kingfish in a coconut-milk gravy with tamarind, curry leaves and spices. Bengali-style versions with mustard and turmeric are also common.
how_to_eat: Eat it with steamed rice and papad.
how_to_order: Ask for the day's fish curry with rice at local eateries and beach shacks.

name: Grilled Lobster
description: Lobster split and grilled over an open flame with butter, garlic, chilli and lemon, or in a tandoori marinade. It is the islands' premium seafood dish.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot, squeezing lemon over the meat.
how_to_order: Ask for grilled lobster at seafood grills in Port Blair or Havelock; price depends on size.

name: Coconut Prawn Curry
description: Prawns simmered in coconut milk with turmeric, mustard seeds and curry leaves. It is milder than most island curries.
how_to_order: Ask for prawn coconut curry at local restaurants in Neil, Havelock or Port Blair.

name: Chilli Crab
description: Crab cooked in a spicy, slightly tangy sauce of garlic, chillies, onion and tomato. It is served at street-side stalls and restaurants alike.
how_to_eat: Crack the shells by hand and eat with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for chilli crab at seafood restaurants; the price depends on crab size.

name: Andaman Fish Fry
description: Fish shallow-fried with turmeric, chilli, salt and lime, lighter than heavily battered versions. It is sold at small local restaurants and beach stalls.
how_to_eat: Eat it with a squeeze of lime, on its own or with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for the day's fish fry at local eateries.

name: Seafood Thali
description: A full plate of rice, fish fry, fish curry, dal, vegetables and chutneys, with crab, prawn or squid depending on the day's catch. It is a way to try much of the island cuisine in one meal.
how_to_eat: Mix each curry with rice, one at a time.
how_to_order: Ask for a fish or seafood thali at lunchtime in local restaurants.

name: Kewadi
description: A traditional Nicobarese sweet made from the pulp of pandanus fruit (Pandanus leram): the fruit is heated, the pulp scraped out, kneaded into dough, rolled, wrapped in leaves and cooked again. Making it is a communal activity, especially at festivals.
how_to_eat: Eat it as a sweet at Nicobarese gatherings.
